nodes.label: tests workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs the unit / multi-node / smoke suite plus the README-badge updater, triggering on any change that could plausibly affect a test result - source, ANY test subtree including integration (shared helpers there could shift unit-test imports), dependency manifest, tsconfig. Docs, README, ROADMAP and CHANGELOG changes deliberately skip. The concurrency group is keyed on github.ref with cancel-in-progress only for pull requests: develop pushes queue so every commit's README state lands in order, PR re-pushes cancel stale work.

nodes.label: Single coverage run test job
nodes.rationale: Typechecks, runs the suite ONCE with --coverage and parses the stats out of that single run. It used to run twice - a test job without coverage, then an update-readme job with it - which gave the parser a different bun output than the one the build status came from, so a flaky timing-sensitive test under coverage instrumentation could push the badge to 1489 of 1490 while the build stayed green. One run, one source of truth; the badge job consumes these outputs and re-runs nothing.

nodes.label: JUnit-report test-count parser
nodes.rationale: bun's output goes to a FILE, never through a pipe: under Actions bun emits one annotation line per test (~8700 here) and a command-substitution pipe made bun die mid-flush with WriteFailed, truncating the coverage table and taking the JUnit report with it. Counts come from the JUnit root element, not the console - Bun 1.3.14 stopped printing the trailing summary block, so the old grep matched nothing, and what made it ship was a fallback turning parser-found-nothing into a plausible zero that published a tests-0 of 0 badge from a green run. Hence both halves: read a contract that does not move between releases, and treat an unreadable count as an error rather than as zero. Skipped tests are subtracted so total means actually-executed. bun's exit status is replayed at the end so the job's own result is unchanged.

nodes.label: Coverage-floor gate (>= 80%)
nodes.rationale: Line coverage is read from the All files aggregate row (awk field 3, since column 2 is % Funcs) and the floor lives in COVERAGE_LINE_FLOOR so tightening it is a one-line change. The two statistics fail differently on purpose: an unparseable coverage figure fails the step, because a skipped gate must not read as a passing one, while an unparseable test count only annotates a warning - main is branch-protected on this check and a cosmetic parse failure must never block a release. 80 is pragmatic: the quarantined worker-thread suites remove coverage of the worker machinery and drop hosted-CI coverage to ~86%, and raising the floor is part of un-quarantining.

nodes.label: ACTOR_TS_SKIP_FLAKY_MNS quarantine flag
nodes.rationale: Quarantines the worker-thread multi-node suites (ParallelMultiNodeSpec, ParallelPubSub) and the in-process LeaseMajority e2e on GitHub's hosted runners, where Bun cannot respawn functional worker threads after the first test - which also starves lease arbitration into a false split-brain. They run locally and in Docker, and the real-network integration workflow is the multi-node CI gate; nightly-flakes.yml runs the three with the flag OFF and carries the exit criterion (#538).

nodes.label: README badge updater job
nodes.rationale: The only job in the workflow that can write to the repository and deliberately the only one that runs no third-party code: it installs nothing, builds nothing, re-runs nothing - it consumes the test job's parsed numbers, rewrites README.md with sed and pushes. It runs on !cancelled() rather than success(), because a red suite is exactly when the badge must flip to red, and only for develop pushes. A plausibility check rejects missing, non-numeric or zero counts and leaves the previous figures with a warning - the earlier guard only asked whether numbers were present, and a zero is present. Values reach the script through env:, never as ${{ }} pasted into the shell.

nodes.label: persist-credentials: false on installing jobs
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the test job talks to the remote and bun.lock has no git-protocol dependencies, so the pushable credential a checkout leaves in .git/config is pure attack surface for the ~2000 packages installed one step later. Before the split, contents: write plus a persisted credential sat in the same job that executed the whole devDependency tree, so any postinstall script or compromised transitive package could have pushed to develop (#622).
